title: Lavender Tallow Balm: The Weird Thing I Put on My Face That Actually Worked
body:
Okay so. My skin was just being a jerk this spring. Like, it was 73 degrees out but my face thought it was still February in Alaska. Dry patches. This weird tight feeling. I was using that fancy La Mer cream my sister gave me for Christmas—the tiny jar that costs more than my car payment—and it was doing nothing. Absolutely nothing. It just sat there. Like a fancy, expensive film. I was at the Walgreens on 5th, not the one by the highway, staring at the Cetaphil shelf for like 20 minutes. My phone was at 12%. I just felt defeated.

Then this algorithm thing, you know how it is, showed me a video. Someone was talking about putting beef fat on their face. Beef fat. I was eating pretzels. I almost choked. I clicked anyway because what else was I gonna do, my show was buffering.

**How I Ended Up Buying Beef Tallow for My Skin**

The whole thing sounded insane. But the person in the video, she wasn't all glow-y and fake. She was like, “Look, I know this sounds gross, but my eczema is gone.” And she had this little jar of whipped stuff that looked like butter. I fell down a rabbit hole. It was a Tuesday night, maybe 11:47 PM. I learned that tallow—that’s the beef fat—from grass-fed cows is apparently really similar to the oils our own skin makes. Our skin recognizes it or something. Absorbs it deep instead of just sitting on top. The one I kept seeing was this **Whipped Tallow Balm** from some small shop in France, made with lavender. For sleep and anxiety. I was skeptical. So skeptical. But also, my credit card was already out. The La Mer was a lost cause. What’s another forty-something bucks?

It arrived two weeks later in this unassuming little box. I opened it on my kitchen counter. The jar was heavier than I thought. I unscrewed the lid.

Here’s where I expected to be horrified. I thought it would smell like a barn. Or raw meat. Or something deeply, profoundly wrong.

It didn’t. It smelled like… lavender. But not like a candle. Or a cleaning product. Just like lavender. The real plant. Maybe a little earthy underneath? I don’t know how to describe it. It was calming. Simple. The texture was weird. Not bad weird. It was solid but soft, like cold butter straight from the fridge, but if you push your finger in it gives way. It’s whipped, so it’s got this airy feel. I put a tiny bit on the back of my hand. It was cool. Then it just… vanished. My skin drank it. No greasy film. No shiny residue. Just my skin, but softer. Huh.

**What This Lavender Tallow Balm Actually Does**

So my **natural skincare routine** was a joke before. It was a graveyard of expensive bottles under my sink. Things with acids and retinol and names I couldn’t pronounce. They’d make my skin red or peel-y or just angry. This was the opposite.

I started using it at night. After I wash my face, I scoop out a little—like half a pea size—warm it between my fingers, and press it into my skin. Don’t rub, just press. The smell is the first thing. It’s not strong. It’s just there. And it does something. My brain goes, “Oh, bedtime.” I watch my shows with it on. My cat tries to sniff my face. It’s become this whole little ritual.

It doesn’t “do” ten things. It does one thing, really well: it makes my skin not feel like it’s going to crack open. The dry patches on my cheeks? Gone in like four days. The fine lines around my eyes—I’m 36, they’re there—look less… thirsty. They’re not gone, let’s be real, nothing is magic. But they’re softer. Like the skin there is just more comfortable. It’s not a dramatic transformation. It’s a quiet one. My skin just finally shut up and stopped complaining.

**My Skin After a Few Weeks of Tallow Balm Daily Use**

I’ve been using it for maybe a month now? **Switching to natural products** felt weird at first because I was so used to that chemical smell, that instant tingle that’s supposed to mean it’s working. This doesn’t tingle. It just… works.

The best proof? My elbows. Random, I know. But they’re always rough. Like sandpaper. I put some of the balm on them one night because I had extra on my hands. Just on a whim. For three nights. And now they’re… smooth. Not baby smooth, that’s a lie. But normal-person smooth. I didn’t even know they could do that. My hands don’t crack between the knuckles anymore when I make a fist. It’s the little things.

I got my mom one. She has psoriasis on her hands, the really dry, flaky kind. She called me last week. She was like, “What is in this stuff? The redness is down.” She’s a tough sell. She uses it now. I’m on my second jar. I got it from the same little Etsy shop, “PureFil” I think it’s called. The shipping took a bit again but whatever, it’s coming from France.

**Would I Buy This Lavender Tallow Balm Again?**

Yeah. I already did.

Look, it’s not for everyone. If you want a fancy jar with a gold spoon and a 12-step promise, this ain’t it. It’s beef fat and lavender in a glass jar. It sounds weird when you say it out loud. But my skin hasn’t felt this normal, this just *okay*, in years. It doesn’t feel stressed. I don’t stress about it. That’s the real result.

It’s just a simple thing that does what it says. My face feels calm. I smell lavender before bed. My elbows are presentable. That’s it. That’s the whole review.

Anyway, if your skin is being difficult and all the regular stuff just makes it worse, this might be worth a shot. It’s one of those things you have to try to get it. I didn’t get it until I tried it.

---

### Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, surprisingly. The science-y reason is that the fat molecules in grass-fed tallow are really close to the oils our own skin produces. So your skin recognizes it and absorbs it properly, instead of it just clogging stuff up. It’s like giving your skin something it actually knows how to use.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not in my experience. And I can get clogged pores pretty easy. Because it absorbs so deeply, it doesn’t just sit on top of your skin forming a greasy layer. It sinks in. My face actually feels less congested since I switched.

**What does the lavender tallow balm smell like?**
Just lavender. Not fake or perfume-y. Like if you crushed the actual dried flowers in your hand. It’s earthy and herbal and really calming. It’s not strong at all once it’s on your skin, just a soft scent that fades as you fall asleep.
